issues.question: Will Berkeley's stormwater plans account for high Bay water coming up the drains?

responsibleAgencies.name: City of Berkeley Public Works
responsibleAgencies.role: Is updating the Stormwater Master Plan, which includes the City's hydraulic model of the storm drains, condition and capacity assessments and capital priorities. The work plan gives January 2024 to December 2026 and $2,000,000; the CIP expects completion in FY 2027 (D11).

responsibleAgencies.name: City of Berkeley Parks, Recreation and Waterfront
responsibleAgencies.role: Holds a $4,122,000 California Transportation Commission grant for the Aquatic Park Tide Tube Replacement and Dredging Project (D11). The lagoon's tide tubes have sliding gates the City keeps open to the tide (D7).

responsibleAgencies.name: Berkeley City Council
responsibleAgencies.role: Adopted the FY 2027–2031 Capital Improvement Program, which funds both projects, on 2026-06-23 (Resolution No. 72,340–N.S.; D11).

issues.decision: Two City projects already under way will shape how west Berkeley's drains meet the Bay. The Stormwater Master Plan's published scope covers the hydraulic model, the pipes' condition and capacity, and capital priorities, and leaves out Bay tides, outfalls, tide gates and sea level rise (D11). The Aquatic Park tide tube replacement is funded, and its design is unpublished.

alternatives.label: Have the Stormwater Master Plan test high Bay water at the outfalls
alternatives.detail: Run the City's hydraulic model with the Bay at today's storm tides and at the sea level rise levels the City already uses, list which outfalls have tide gates and their condition, and publish the results with the plan.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Adds scope and cost to a plan due in FY 2027. In return the City's hydraulic model, with real pipes and outfalls, replaces this explorer's assumption of open outfalls.

alternatives.label: Design the new tide tubes to close ahead of a storm tide
alternatives.detail: Keep the tidal exchange the tubes were restored for (D7), and add gates that can be shut before a storm tide, with a written plan for when to shut and reopen them.
alternatives.tradeoffs: A shut gate holds rain in the lagoon. In 2023 the City Manager wrote that failed tubes had meant regular flooding at the lagoon in heavy rains (D7). Closing ahead of a storm tide takes a forecast and staff on hand. Cost unknown.

alternatives.label: Proceed as scoped
alternatives.detail: Finish both projects as described: the master plan keeps its published scope, and the tubes are replaced and the lagoon dredged with the gates run as they are now.
alternatives.tradeoffs: No added cost or delay. The high-water question stays open, and the explorer's results stay a range between gates open and gates closed.

evidenceGaps.why: The model places one outfall per watershed at the cell nearest open water (D3).
They decide at what Bay level water enters each pipe and how long the tide holds it shut.
Which outfalls have working gates decides whether the teal ground can fill at all (D6, C9).
The model assumes every inlet connects to its watershed's outfall (D6). The City's hydraulic model holds the real network, unpublished (D11).
The 2023 work orders record backups in rain (D5).

evidenceGaps.item: Aquatic Park lagoon levels and gate settings
evidenceGaps.why: Whether the lagoon follows the Bay at a storm tide (D9).
